findings.quote: So this Olympiad year was drawing to a close.
findings.problem: The Greek opens with only the tail of a sentence from the preceding (lost/cut) chapter: ὀλυμπιάδος. There is no verb and no 'year drawing to a close'; the English invents a complete sentence and smooths the break.

units.note: Rest of chapter checked: numbers (3000 chalkaspides, 2000 peltasts, 300 Cretans, 400 horse), Aratus the elder, solstice all correct.
Numbers (two lochoi, 2200, 100 horse) correct. Greek has Φενικῆς (probably Pheneus/Pheneatis); English 'Pheneus' acceptable.
'share a political alliance' for πολιτεύεσθαι is loose (political union) but not wrong in sense; not flagged.
καθ' ὅσον ... κατὰ τοσοῦτον correlative rendered correctly.

findings.problem: Πυθίαν Πελληνέα: a man of Pellene (Achaean city), not Pallene (Chalcidic place).
The Greek name is Πρόσλαον (accusative of Πρόσλαος), i.e. Proslaus, not Prolaus.
